title: Spam Burst Detection Window
real_world_story: Public chat rooms and live gaming streams are frequently targeted by spam bots broadcasting repetitive links. The automated abuse prevention system monitors message timestamp streams. If a user posts more than L messages in any continuous time window of width W seconds, the system flags the user for a temporary rate-limit mute.
problem_statement: Given a sequence of N message timestamps t_1, t_2, ..., t_N in strictly ascending chronological order (in seconds) sent by a user, a window duration W, and a spam threshold limit L, find the maximum number of messages sent within any continuous sliding interval of at most W seconds (i.e., t_j - t_i <= W). Output the maximum message count and either 'ALERT' (if max count > L) or 'OK' (if max count <= L), separated by a space.
task: Compute the maximum number of messages in any sliding time window of length W and determine whether it exceeds threshold L.
input_format:
The first line contains three space-separated integers N, W, and L, denoting the number of messages, window duration in seconds, and threshold limit.
The second line contains N space-separated integers t_1, t_2, ..., t_N representing timestamps in strictly increasing order.
output_format: Print the maximum number of messages found in any window of duration W, followed by a space and 'ALERT' if the count exceeds L, or 'OK' otherwise.

examples.explanation: For window starting at t=1, timestamps {1, 3, 5, 6} have span 6 - 1 = 5 <= 5, giving 4 messages. Since 4 > L=3, the status is ALERT.
All consecutive timestamps differ by 15 seconds. Every window of width 10 seconds contains at most 1 message. Since 1 <= L=5, the status is OK.

real_world_takeaway: Two-pointer sliding window algorithms evaluate dynamic rate limiting over timestamp streams in linear time with minimal memory overhead.
